project.title: The Legal Last Mile
project.subtitle: Sanitation governance and administrative law in Brazil, Canada (Ontario) and the Netherlands
project.institution: Doctoral application in progress (target institution: Erasmus University Rotterdam; not yet confirmed)
project.summary: An interactive laboratory for a comparative doctoral project on the gap between legal obligations to provide sanitation and actual access to services. Early-stage: the thesis does not yet exist. This site currently shows one reproduction audit of preliminary validation work, one synthetic software demonstration, and the structure for evidence and comparison.
project.citation: Klaus, J. (2026) Thesis2Lab: The Legal Last Mile laboratory (software, version 0.1.0). Not yet archived; no DOI.
project.disclaimer: Research in progress. Nothing on this site is legal advice. Results labelled exploratory or synthetic are not findings. Scientific and legal conclusions require researcher review.

cover.title: Read this first
cover.lead: This is an exploration, not a finished study. It shows what a doctoral research project could look like when every claim can be traced and every number can be recomputed, and it is honest about how much is still missing.

sections.heading: What this is
body: Thesis2Lab turns a research project into an interactive laboratory that runs in an ordinary web browser. Readers can follow a claim back to its source, change the settings of an analysis, compare the result with the original, and download a record of what was run.

The first project is a proposed doctoral study of sanitation governance and administrative law in Brazil, Ontario and the Netherlands. The aim of this site is to test whether that kind of research can be made inspectable, not to present findings.

sections.heading: It is based on partial studies
body: Everything here rests on early, incomplete work. Please read results with that in mind.
bullets: The thesis has not been written, and the doctoral application is still in progress. Chapters shown are working labels, not a plan.
The only authentic analysis is a reproduction check on 91 court decisions (71 Dutch, 20 Brazilian) taken from the author's preliminary validation work. No Canadian decisions are included.
The large court-decision dataset behind the preliminary research is not included, so the experiment that depends on it is blocked.
The bibliometric explorer uses invented data. It demonstrates the software and says nothing about real literature.
The comparative governance matrix holds the author's own hypotheses and one reported search result. It contains no verified statements of law yet.
Every claim is marked unreviewed by the researcher, and no independent human review has been recorded.

sections.heading: Why explore this in this subject
body: Research on sanitation law and administrative law often relies on coded court decisions and on comparisons across legal systems. Readers rarely get to check how the coding was done or whether the published figures can be recomputed.

The subject is also about the gap between what the law promises and what people can actually reach. A research format that shows its working, including where numbers do not match, suits a field concerned with that gap. This project is a way to learn whether the approach is useful before the thesis depends on it.

sections.heading: What AI was used for
body: The laboratory was designed, coded, tested and documented in one working session with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code), following written rules that put scientific integrity ahead of speed. The author set the goals and remains responsible for the research.
bullets: Building: the website, the data checks, the tests and the documentation.

Auditing: the build recomputed the published agreement figures and found inconsistencies in the source material, such as two different confidence intervals for the same quantity and a headline figure with no output file behind it.
Verifying: every calculation was written twice, once for the site and once independently in Python, then compared.
Earlier work: the second coder in the 91-decision audit was itself a language model. That makes it a reproducibility check on a keyword filter, not human inter-coder reliability.

sections.heading: What AI is not doing here
body: Visiting this site does not call any AI service. Every number comes from a fixed calculation that runs on your own device, so the same inputs always give the same results.
bullets: AI did not conduct legal research or reach legal conclusions.
AI-written text and code are not treated as verified scholarship. A status label is shown only when a recorded test run supports it.
AI can be wrong. The checks, the stale-report detection and the pending human review exist for that reason.

sections.heading: How to read the site
body: Each experiment carries a status. Exploratory means a demonstration. Partially reproduced means some published numbers were recomputed and some could not be. Blocked means something required is missing. A synthetic data banner appears wherever invented data are used.

sections.heading: What would make it stronger
bullets: A human second coder on a sample of the decisions.
The raw decision data, or a cleared subset, with redistribution terms confirmed.
Real bibliographic records for the literature review.
Verified legal sources for the comparative matrix.
Researcher review of each claim and a named independent reviewer for each experiment.
body: Each of these would move an experiment up the status ladder or remove a limitation.
